sasha: Console shows p99 for /v1/generate = ~180ms but API raw telemetry p99 is ~420ms for the same 15m window. Anyone seeing this? cc @mike :thinking:

mike: Are you comparing the endpoint-level time-series vs the route rollup? The Console aggregates by route and uses per-shard t-digest merges by default. Can you paste the exact query or screenshot?

sasha: here's the query I'm running in the console:
```
SELECT approx_percentile(0.99, latency_ms) FROM request_latency
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND ts >= now()-15m
GROUP BY route
```
This returns ~180ms. The raw API telemetry (per-request) shows a 99th closer to 420ms.

anna: If you're merging t-digests without incorporating sample counts you can get percentile inversion. We recently changed a codepath that did uniform merges when shards had wildly different counts. If `use_count=false` on the merge metadata the result can understate tail.

jordan: Also check routing affinity / cache topology. If warm-cache nodes serve most requests, p50 will look great; p99 comes from cold or slow backends. If rollups mix shards across cache tiers without weights it skews the percentiles.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: telemetry-service v2.4.1 -> canary deployed :rocket:

mike: Short-term mitigation: flip the Console rollup to `weighted_merge=true` and re-run the rollup for the last 1h (or replay raw events). Longer-term: include sample_count in the wire format and fail merges that drop counts. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/4321

sasha: testing weighted merge now... ok that fixed it — p99 ~410ms and matches raw. Thanks, saved my morning :coffee: :thumbsup:
